label: Green Claims Review
description: Review draft advertising copy, packaging or website text against the EU green-claims regime: Directive (EU) 2024/825 amendments to the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC and the Consumer Rights Directive 2011/83/EU, applying from 27 September 2026. Returns a claim-by-claim verdict, the substantiation gap behind each claim, and compliant rewrites.

claudeKnowledge.description: EU green-claims regime: Directive (EU) 2024/825, UCPD 2005/29/EC Annex I and Articles 6-7 as amended, CRD 2011/83/EU information duties, national transposing measures

guidedInputs.label: Draft copy, packaging or website text
guidedInputs.description: Paste the text exactly as it will appear, including headlines, straplines, body copy, on-pack wording, hashtags and any label or logo wording. Every claim is judged on its own words.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. "The eco-friendly choice. Our climate-neutral packaging is made from 100% recycled materials, and we will be net zero by 2035."

guidedInputs.label: Where the claim appears
guidedInputs.description: Determines whether the Consumer Rights Directive pre-contractual information duties are in scope alongside the claim rules.

options.label: Comparison tool, eco-score or ranking feature

guidedInputs.label: Claim types present
guidedInputs.description: Tick what you believe is in the copy. The review checks for all of these regardless, but this focuses the substantiation questions.

options.label: Generic environmental wording (eco, green, sustainable, environmentally friendly)
Sustainability label, trust mark or eco-logo
Future environmental performance pledge (net zero by X)
Recycled content, recyclability or circularity claim
Comparison against other products, brands or suppliers
Compliance with a legal requirement presented as a feature

guidedInputs.label: Substantiation you hold
guidedInputs.description: What evidence sits behind each claim — life-cycle assessments and their scope, certification-scheme documents, third-party verification and whether its findings are published, transition-plan targets and resourcing, spare-parts and update-support schedules. Leave blank to get the gap list.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. "LCA covering packaging only, 2026, not third-party verified. Net-zero target board-approved, plan not published, no external verifier."

guidedInputs.label: Basis of any sustainability label used
guidedInputs.description: Annex I point 2a prohibits displaying a sustainability label that is neither based on a certification scheme nor established by public authorities.

options.label: No label or trust mark used
Established by public authorities (e.g. EU Ecolabel)
Own / self-declared label or in-house mark
Not sure what sits behind it

guidedInputs.label: Markets in scope
guidedInputs.description: The Directive is transposed market by market. Naming the markets lets the review flag where a national measure has to be checked.

guidedInputs.label: Product or service
guidedInputs.description: Used to test whether a claimed feature is in fact a legal requirement for the whole category, which Annex I point 10a prohibits presenting as distinctive.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. household detergent, running shoes, laptop, energy tariff

guidedInputs.label: Planned launch or live date
guidedInputs.description: The same wording is judged differently before and from 27 September 2026, the date from which Member States apply the transposing measures.

exampleInput:
Review the launch copy for our new laundry detergent range before it goes live across Sweden, Germany and the Netherlands.

Headline: "The eco-friendly way to wash."
Strapline: "Climate-neutral cleaning, guaranteed."
Body: "Our new EcoPure range is kinder to the planet. The bottle is made from 100% recycled plastic and is fully recyclable. All emissions from production are offset through certified forestry projects, making every wash climate neutral. Phosphate-free, as always. We will be a net-zero business by 2035."
On-pack: a green leaf roundel reading "EcoPure Certified" — this is our own mark, designed in-house.

What we hold: a life-cycle assessment from this year covering the bottle only, not third-party verified; offset purchase certificates from the forestry provider; a board-approved net-zero target with no published implementation plan and no external verifier.
